title: Upgrade Orchestration Playbook — SLA & Private Pathways
body:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for running coordinated upgrade/expansion motions during and between QBRs. Focus: upsells from Hosted -> Dedicated, Dedicated -> Private (VPC/on-prem), and premium SLA add-ons. Designed for CSAs, AMs, Solutions Eng, and Sales.

Audience and when to use:
- Use at renewal windows, post-QBRs, and when usage patterns indicate sustained growth or regulatory triggers.
- Primary owners: CSA (engagement + business case), Solutions Eng (technical validation), Sales (commercial negotiation), Finance/Legal (terms).

One-line value prop to customers (internal elevator pitch):
"Move to Dedicated or Private to get predictable latency, dedicated capacity, and enterprise-grade controls — we help you migrate with a low-risk pilot and transparent unit economics."

QBR expansion agenda (30–45m slot to surface expansion):
1) Snapshot (3m) — usage trend, top endpoints by tokens, latency percentile, cost per 1M tokens.
2) Business outcomes (7m) — product metrics impacted by LLM features, revenue or retention signals tied to LLM behavior.
3) Technical fit check (7m) — current throughput, peak concurrency, KV cache hit-rate, model variants in use.
4) Economics and friction (7m) — current unit cost, burst/capacity pain points, compliance needs.
5) Proposed path & ask (6m) — recommend Dedicated or Private + SLA tier, pilot scope, timeline, next MRs.
6) Decision/Next steps (5m) — immediate actions, owner, and date.

Mini renewal tracker (paste into your tracker sheet):
- Customer: {CUSTOMER_NAME}
- Renewal date: {YYYY-MM-DD}
- Current tier: Hosted / Dedicated / Private
- ARR: {ARR}
- Usage trend (3mo): +X%
- Recommended motion: Dedicated reserve / Private pilot / SLA upgrade
- Pilot start target: {YYYY-MM-DD}
- Tech contact: {SE_NAME}
- Commercial owner: {AM_NAME}
- Risk flags: data residency, SOC2/HIPAA, budget cycle, procurement windows

Play phases (detailed):
1) Qualification (owner: CSA)
  - Trigger signals: sustained >20% month-over-month token growth, repeated latency SLO violations, security/compliance ask, forecasted ARR lift > $50k/year or enterprise procurement inbound.
  - CSA checklist: confirm procurement timeline, org stakeholder map, high-level cost tolerance, and any regulatory constraints.

2) Scoping and Commercial Proposal (owner: AM + CSA)
  - Create a two-tier offer: a) 6–8 week pilot (discounted Dedicated/Private staging) b) 12–24 month committed capacity with defined throughput and SLA.
  - Pricing cheat sheet: show delta vs hosted unit price, estimated ROI with queuing/burst reductions, and break-even month.
  - Deliverable: one-pager commercial memo + pilot SOW draft.

3) Technical Validation (owner: Solutions Eng)
  - Run a smoke pilot: mirror top 5 production prompts, measure p95 latency, batch effectiveness, and KV cache warmup time.
  - Security checklist for Private: VPN/VPC peering, KMS integration, audit log shipping, HSM/KMS cert exchange.
  - Deliverable: pilot runbook and short triage report (p95, tokens/sec, errors).

4) Contracting and Legal (owner: AM + Legal)
  - Include: SLA terms (uptime + latency targets), support response times, data-handling annex, termination/rollback clauses, and onboarding milestones.
  - Typical redlines to expect: data deletion timelines, subcontractor disclosures, and incident notification windows.

5) Migration & Rollout (owner: SE + SRE + Customer)
  - Rollout runbook: pre-cutover checklist, smoke tests, traffic split strategy (canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%), rollback plan.
  - Monitoring: per-route latency dashboards, token cost estimates, error rates, and user-facing feature health.

6) Post-migration QBR and expansion close-out (owner: CSA)
  - Validate SLA metrics, adoption lift (feature usage), cost delta vs projection, and a handoff to Success for ongoing optimization.

Customer-facing templates (short snippets you can copy):
Email subject: "Proposal: Dedicated capacity pilot to stabilize latency & reduce per-token cost"
Email body:
Hi {Name},

Based on our last QBR and your recent traffic, we recommend a short Dedicated pilot to address the latency spikes and predictable throughput needs. Pilot outline:
- 6 weeks, dedicated pool sized for your p95 demand
- Measured goals: p95 < target, reduced token queuing, and 95% reduction in tail errors
- Outcome: economic comparison and production rollout plan

Can we sync next week to align on pilot scope and timelines?

Best,
{AM_NAME}

Discovery call script (3 questions to surface blockers):
1) "If we could guarantee p95 latency at X ms and a committed pool, how would your product roadmaps change?"
2) "What internal procurement or security approvals are required for a private deployment?"
3) "Are there any integration points (KMS, SIEM, SI) that would lengthen deployment?"

Risk matrix (quick):
- Procurement delay -> mitigation: offer pilot on existing contract and start technical validation.
- Data residency/regulatory hold -> mitigation: propose Private with required data flow diagram and early legal engagement.
- Unexpected cost delta -> mitigation: conservative sizing + monthly cost review and automated throttling rules.

Operational runbook highlights (Dedicated vs Private differences):
- Dedicated: faster time-to-pilot, no network onboarding, typical 2–4 week technical ramp. Key checks: autoscale headroom, reserve config, burst policies.
- Private: involves networking change windows, KMS/HSM integration, and customer change control. Typical 6–12 week ramp. Key checks: VPC peering tests, cert exchanges, and compliance attestations.

KPIs to present in QBRs for expansion justification:
- Tokens/month growth (3mo and 12mo)
- P95 and P99 latency pre/post pilot
- Cache hit-rate improvement with dedicated pooling
- Error & rate-limit incident count reduction
- Estimated monthly cost delta and projected ROI

Internal handoffs & RACI (short):
- CSA: champion, customer context, business case owner
- AM: commercial terms, contracting
- SE: pilot design, technical commit, cutover lead
- SRE: monitoring, escalation
- Legal: contract terms and compliance review

Open questions / TODOs (work-in-progress):
- Need an updated pricing calculator for Dedicated burst vs reserved profiles (ask Revenue Ops).
- Template SOW for Private deployments: draft skeleton in Confluence, needs Legal sign-off.
- Playbook checklist needs a short 1-page customer-facing brochure (DE/Marketing).

Examples of success stories to cite in QBRs (quick bullets):
- Retail customer reduced checkout latency by 45% and cut per-token cost by 30% after a 12-month Dedicated commit.
- Healthcare pilot achieved SOC2 evidence flow and migrated sensitive PII workloads into Private within 8 weeks.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the QBR ask crisp: state the business outcome first, then the technical justification, then the commercial ask.
- Use cost delta instead of raw price when talking to finance stakeholders.
- For non-technical execs, swap latency percentiles for "time to response" language and impact on conversion/SLAs.

Appendix: quick checklists (copyable)
- Pilot readiness checklist: traffic sample, top-5 prompts, monitoring creds, test accounts, rollback window.
- Legal pack: draft SOW, data annex, security questionnaire answers, certs.

End of draft playbook.

Recent changes log:
- 2024-11-08: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2024-12-03: added technical validation checklist (Marco)
- 2025-03-12: pricing notes and email templates added (Janelle)

Unresolved: get Revenue Ops pricing calc + confirm typical SLA wording for latency (p95 vs p99) to include in commercial template.
